scenario.title: Round-trip airport, layover, duration, and destination changes
scenario.focus: Round-trip context retention, airport and layover filters, compound removals, filter-then-read sequencing, flexible-date search, and destination changes.

turns.user: Find round-trip business-class flights from Los Angeles to New York, leaving October 30, 2026 and returning November 6, 2026, for two adults.
turns.expectedIntent: Start a complete exact-date round-trip search.
turns.why: Both route endpoints, both dates, passenger count, trip type, and cabin are known.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a round-trip search with no active filters.
turns.validates: Round-trip payload assembly and Manager-to-Flight context handoff.

turns.user: Use Burbank departures, arrive at Newark, allow one stop, require checked baggage, and keep layovers under two hours.
turns.expectedIntent: Apply departure airport, arrival airport, stops, baggage, and layover-duration filters together.
turns.why: These constrain existing results and should be one filter call even if the combination has no matches.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key and activate five filter categories.
turns.validates: Full compound airport/filter payload and correct zero-result state retention.

turns.user: Remove Newark and checked baggage. Allow any Los Angeles-area departure airport, require a Dubai or Amsterdam layover, and arrive in the evening.
turns.expectedIntent: Remove two filters, broaden one airport filter, and add layover-airport plus arrival-time constraints.
turns.why: The search inputs are unchanged; all operations belong in one state-aware filter update.
turns.expectedStateChange: Preserve one stop and layover duration, replace departure-airport scope, remove arrival airport and baggage, and add layover airport plus evening arrival.
turns.validates: Multiple removals/additions, named airport-group resolution, alternative layover airports, and active-filter preservation.

turns.user: Make arrival morning instead, cap total duration at three hours, and remove both the layover-airport restriction and the layover-duration limit.
turns.expectedIntent: Replace arrival time, add total duration, and remove two layover filters.
turns.why: This changes only filters and must preserve the departure-airport and one-stop constraints.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep departureAirport, stops, morning arrival, and totalDuration filters.
turns.validates: Changing an applied filter and removing multiple related filters in one call.

turns.user: Remove the one-stop filter too. Which options remain, and which is shortest?
turns.expectedIntent: Remove stops, then inspect the newly filtered current result set.
turns.why: The filter mutation must finish before current-option facts and ranking are read.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the same search key with departureAirport, morning arrival, and total duration active.
turns.validates: Filter-then-read sequencing and no re-search for current-result reasoning.

turns.user: Find stronger round-trip departure dates between November 1 and November 5, returning exactly seven days later, then show flights for the strongest date. Keep only morning arrival and total duration under three hours.
turns.expectedIntent: Predict within a bounded round-trip window, search the strongest or fallback pair, then apply only two carried filters.
turns.why: Flexible outbound timing plus a fixed stay requires round-trip prediction before search, and the new result set must be filtered afterward.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a new search key and retain only arrivalTime and totalDuration filters.
turns.validates: Round-trip prediction bounds/duration, serial dependency handling, and explicit filter carry-forward.

turns.user: Keep those dates, passengers, and cabin, but fly to Boston instead. Do not keep any filters.
turns.expectedIntent: Change the destination and run a clean new search using all other established search inputs.
turns.why: Destination is a core search field; the explicit no-filters instruction means no apply_filter call is needed after the new search clears state.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a Boston search key with no active filters.
turns.validates: Route update versus filtering, round-trip context reuse, and clean filter reset through new-search semantics.
